topic: Construction and navigation of critical aircraft wiring systems
syllabus_extract: Construction and navigation of critical aircraft wiring systems

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of wiring schematics and identification of critical system components; Safety: Ensure no live power sources are present; Supervision: Instructor verifies schematic interpretation accuracy
intro_questions: What does the acronym EWIS stand for?
Why is the wiring system considered a critical aircraft system?
What are the primary functions of the aircraft electrical power distribution system?

development.content:
Definition and scope of EWIS
Components of the wiring system
Routing and bundling standards
Identification of critical systems
Navigation of wiring diagrams

Wiring harness construction methods
Conduit and protective covering types
Termination and connector standards
Grounding and bonding practices
Labeling and identification codes

Inspection criteria for critical wiring
Common defects and failure modes
Documentation of wiring issues
Maintenance procedures for EWIS
Safety implications of wiring faults

summary_questions: Explain the difference between a standard wiring harness and a critical system wiring bundle.
Describe the steps required to navigate a complex wiring diagram for a critical system.
Identify three common defects that could compromise the integrity of an aircraft wiring system.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief summary of the key differences between LP 02 and this lesson regarding wiring practices, to be discussed in the next session.
